LESSON: WRITING 2.3.1 PUNCTUATION

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.3: Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we punctuate sentences?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify punctuation marks (exclamation marks, double quotation marks and question marks) in a text
2. apply punctuation marks accurately in a text for effective communication
3. appreciate the use of punctuation marks for effective communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: WRITING 2.3.1 PUNCTUATION
This lesson teaches Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation for Grade 5 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

STUDY STEPS
1. identify punctuation marks (exclamation marks, double quotation marks and question marks) in a text
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. apply punctuation marks accurately in a text for effective communication
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
3. appreciate the use of punctuation marks for effective communication
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation above.
2. Explain Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation important for a Grade 5 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we punctuate sentences?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify punctuation marks (exclamation marks, double quotation marks and question marks) in a text
2. apply punctuation marks accurately in a text for effective communication
3. appreciate the use of punctuation marks for effective communication

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
